solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Alastair's outside with joint, meeting Blair where meat is sold

indicators.note: the two pieces meet the wife's name by going into the middle of it

parts.note: Cherie Blair, wife of the former Prime Minister, rather than Tony

indicators.note: the outside of the name Alastair means only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: a joint of meat is a cut

explanation.surface: Alastair Campbell and a Blair meet up with a joint at a butcher's, a picture of New Labour figures out shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' looks like Tony, but it is Cherie, opened up to take AR (Alastair's outside letters) and CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-style delicatessen selling cooked and cured pork products is a place where meat is sold.

clue.text: Lecturer leaves address with this country's uplifting poem

indicators.note: the lecturer leaves, so that letter departs from the greeting word

parts.note: to hail someone is to address them

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting reads the two letters bottom to top

parts.note: for a British setter this country is the UK

explanation.surface: A lecturer walks out of a speech, leaving behind a patriotic poem for the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: HAIL without its L gives HAI; UK turned upwards ('uplifting') gives KU.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese verse form of three lines and seventeen syllables is a short poem.

clue.text: Academic establishment, near to decay, houses famous dictionary

indicators.note: the rearranged letters house the dictionary's initials inside them
letters that decay fall apart and re-form, so the word near is rearranged

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A crumbling college building is home to a celebrated dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to decay' rearranges NEAR into R...EAN, which 'houses' OED. ROEDEAN is a well-known girls' boarding school near Brighton in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous English independent girls' school is an academic establishment.

clue.text: Assuming dog's without lead, it will be grabbed

indicators.note: the word it is grabbed, held inside the shortened dog
losing its lead means the young dog loses its first letter

parts.note: a puppy is a young dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a dog off its lead will be grabbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assuming' is not 'supposing' but an old adjective meaning presumptuous; 'without lead' drops the dog's first letter and 'will be grabbed' puts the pronoun inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Assuming in the old sense of arrogant or presumptuous matches being self-important and above one's station.

clue.text: Falling under river, react broadcasting curse

indicators.note: in a down clue the rearranged letters fall below the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: broadcasting scatters the letters of react into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tumbles into a river and reacts by shouting a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcasting' rearranges the five letters, and in a down clue 'Falling under' places them below the Devon river.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to denounce or call down evil on, a synonym for curse as a verb.

clue.text: Liam's new outside storage space erected wrong

indicators.note: the rearranged name sits outside the upturned memory letters
new signals the name's letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the name Liam, the possessive giving no letter

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means the memory letters are stood upright, read upwards

parts.note: ROM, read-only memory, is a computer's storage

explanation.surface: Liam's new shed has been put up badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the name around the computer memory, which 'erected' turns upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral behaviour is morally wrong, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: State ceremony by church held amongst sculpted statues

parts.note: Mass is a church ceremony

indicators.note: the church abbreviation is held amongst the rearranged letters
sculpted letters are shaped into a new form, so statues is rearranged

explanation.surface: A state ceremony beside a church is surrounded by carved statues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculpted' rearranges the statues, and 'held amongst' puts the church abbreviation inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A New England state of the USA, capital Boston.

clue.text: Incessant university bar, upon retirement, spoiled date

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for bar is read backwards

parts.note: to bar is to ban

indicators.note: spoiled letters are messed up, so date is rearranged

explanation.surface: A university bar endlessly spoils a romantic date when it closes.
explanation.walkthrough: BAN 'upon retirement' becomes NAB; 'spoiled' rearranges DATE into ATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabated means without lessening or pause, which is what incessant describes.

clue.text: Dramatist stood up new books, hardbacks firstly, to impress one undertaking contract?

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so the pieces are pressed inside the killer

parts.note: a jackal is a hired killer, after the assassin in The Day of the Jackal
rose means stood up
NT is the New Testament, the new books of the Bible

indicators.note: firstly takes only the opening letter of hardbacks

explanation.surface: A playwright gets to his feet as new hardback books arrive, hoping to impress a publisher offering a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one undertaking contract' is not a writer signing a deal but a contract killer, as in The Day of the Jackal. Jack Rosenthal was an English TV dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: The English writer of Coronation Street episodes and many television plays was a dramatist.

clue.text: Assistant carries root of bamboo to bear

indicators.note: the assistant carries the letter within itself

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

indicators.note: the root of a word is its start, so only the first letter of bamboo

explanation.surface: A helper hauls a bamboo root along to feed a bear, panda-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like an animal eating bamboo, but it is the verb: to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to tolerate it, a verb synonym for bear.

clue.text: New German doctor blocks pain to treat illness

indicators.note: the German word and the doctor block the rearranged letters, standing in their middle
to treat letters is to work them over, so pain is rearranged

parts.note: neu is the German word for new
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A newly arrived German physician blocks a patient's pain in order to cure a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to treat' rearranges PAIN as P...NIA, and NEU plus MO 'blocks' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the lungs is a serious illness.

clue.text: Battered sweet and sour creates wind

indicators.note: battered letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Battered sweet-and-sour dishes give a diner flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' suggests a Chinese takeaway; it rearranges SWEET and SOUR together.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from the south-west, also the name of a waterproof hat, is a kind of wind.

clue.text: Painter latterly beginning to use ballpoint, we hear. A cubist?

indicators.note: latterly picks out the final letter of painter
the beginning of use is its first letter
we hear signals that the pen brand is rendered by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a Bic is a well-known brand of ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A painter late in life starts using a biro, and so becomes a Cubist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cubist?' is not a Picasso-style painter but the Hungarian inventor of the famous puzzle cube; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Erno Rubik devised the twisting puzzle cube, so playfully he is one who makes cubes.

clue.text: Criminal given punishment (Post Office raids)

indicators.note: the Post Office letters raid, break into, the word for punishment

parts.note: the cane was a school punishment

explanation.surface: A criminal who raids a post office is given a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the Post Office the target of a raid; in fact its letters do the raiding.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster, a famous criminal.

clue.text: Detective and Lieutenant bust site of archaeological hoax

parts.note: PI is a private investigator, a detective
bust means broken, out of action, as down is

explanation.surface: A detective and a police lieutenant raid the scene of an archaeological fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' looks like a police raid, but it means broken, as in a computer being down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sussex place where the fake Piltdown Man skull was found in 1912 is the scene of a famous archaeological fraud.

clue.text: Crossing over, it's authorised to heel

indicators.note: crossing over means the letters of it's go across to the other side, read backwards

parts.note: the letters of it's, the apostrophe ignored
let means allowed or authorised

explanation.surface: A walker crossing a stile is authorised to bring a dog to heel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' tempts as a stile, but 'Crossing over' is the reversal signal on it's.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, high stiletto heel on a woman's shoe is a type of heel.

clue.text: Lane, in films, flanked by court, a royal and religious place

indicators.note: the reporter's first name is flanked, enclosed on each side, by the court letters

parts.note: Lois Lane is Superman's reporter girlfriend in the films
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a royal cipher for the Queen

explanation.surface: A street in a film set runs between a courtyard, a royal residence and a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lane' is not a road but Superman's reporter in the films; 'flanked by' puts her first name between the court letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A covered walkway around a monastery courtyard, or a monastery itself, is a religious place.

clue.text: Tall, up-market fire faces office of bishop

parts.note: U means upper class, up-market

indicators.note: the oven word faces backwards, read right to left

parts.note: to fire pottery is to kiln it
Ely is the see, the seat of office, of a bishop in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A tall, posh fireplace stands opposite a bishop's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tall' is not height but a tall story, one hard to believe; 'faces' turns the oven word backwards. Ely is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an improbable one, so tall here means hard to believe.

clue.text: Breakfast item for those asleep?

parts.note: smoked herrings are a breakfast dish, and people who kip, take a nap, could jokingly be called by the same name

explanation.surface: A breakfast dish meant for people still in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Smoked split herrings are a traditional British breakfast, and the word also suggests people having a kip, slang for a sleep.

clue.text: Models must watch this part of body, cutting back 3/4 of food intake

indicators.note: cutting back means the body part is read backwards

parts.note: a rib is a part of the body

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word drops its last letter

parts.note: a diet is one's food intake

explanation.surface: Fashion models must watch this part of the body, cutting their food intake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models must watch this' looks like the waistline, but photographers tell those posing to 'watch the birdie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers traditionally tell people sitting for a picture to watch the birdie, so it is what posers look at.

clue.text: In command, diver hoisted marine hazard

parts.note: IC means in charge, in command

indicators.note: hoisted in a down clue means the bird's name is lifted, read upwards

parts.note: a grebe is a diving water bird

explanation.surface: A diver in command of a vessel is hoisted out of danger at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diver' is not a person but a diving bird, GREBE, 'hoisted' to read EBERG.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating mass of ice, like the one that sank the Titanic, is a danger to ships at sea.

clue.text: Business rules written by metal pen

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
R is an abbreviation for rule, so two of them for rules
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium, a metal

explanation.surface: Company regulations are written out with a metal-nibbed pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is an enclosure for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure for livestock is a pen, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Finally arrive in some European capital — in Paris

parts.note: en is French for in
du is French for some, as in du pain

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A traveller finally reaches a European capital, namely Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European capital' suggests a city; 'in Paris' marks EN and DU as French words, and 'capital' takes P from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up somewhere is to reach it in the end, an idiom for eventually arriving.

clue.text: Diner, too drunk to eat menu's last item, settled

indicators.note: the mixed letters eat, take inside, the single letter
drunk letters stagger into a new order, so diner and too are mixed
the last item of the word menu is its final letter

explanation.surface: A diner too drunk to manage the last course on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges DINER TOO, which 'to eat' takes in U, the last letter of menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispute that has been ironed out is resolved or settled.

clue.text: In hindsight, some regret touching aquatic animal

indicators.note: In hindsight says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Looking back, someone regrets touching a creature in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A river mammal with webbed feet that hunts fish is an aquatic animal.

clue.text: Heard one saying 'cheers' somewhere in East Midlands

indicators.note: heard signals that the word for the person toasting is taken by its sound

parts.note: someone raising a glass and saying cheers proposes a toast, a toaster

explanation.surface: Someone is overheard saying cheers in a pub in the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: The town is pronounced like 'toaster'. It is a market town in Northamptonshire, an East Midlands county of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Northamptonshire market town known for its racecourse is a place in the East Midlands.

clue.text: Too wide?

definitions.meaning: too means also, in addition, as an additional item
in cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of reach, which earns the batting side a bonus run

explanation.surface: A short complaint that something is too broad.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a wide is one of the bonus runs not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Too means additionally, and a cricket wide is one of the runs given as a bonus outside the batsman's score.

clue.text: Star students, sat around, look overawed by legendary dancer

indicators.note: around signals the letters of sat are turned about into a new order
the word for look is overawed, surrounded and dominated, by the dancer's name

parts.note: Ginger Rogers, Fred Astaire's dancing partner
lo means look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Top pupils sit in a circle, gazing in awe at a famous dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star students' looks like brilliant pupils, but means people who study the stars; 'around' rearranges sat and 'overawed by' sets the look word inside the dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who study the stars and planets to forecast human affairs are students of the stars.
